copyright: Colourful homes line Nyhavn Canal, Copenhagen, Denmark (© emicristea/Getty Images)
description: In Copenhagen, Nyhavn Canal is a burst of colour and history. In Denmark's capital, bright, gabled houses lean toward the water, their reflections rippling beside old wooden ships. Carved out in the 1670s under King Christian V, this 17th-century canal once served as a busy gateway where cargo vessels unloaded goods straight into the city's heart. Sailors crowded its taverns, and the harbour gained a rough reputation long before it became the postcard-perfect place seen today.

copyright: Joshua Tree National Park, California, United States (© JJ Landscapes/Getty Images)
description: Where two great deserts meet, Joshua Tree National Park reveals a stark, mesmerising landscape shaped by wind, time and extremes. In Southern California, the higher Mojave Desert merges with the hotter, lower Colorado Desert, creating a unique blend of ecosystems and remarkable biodiversity.

copyright: Jean-Marie Tjibaou Cultural Centre, New Caledonia (© Fabien Astre/Alamy)
copyrightKeyword: International Day of the Worlds Indigenous Peoples
description: Today, the International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples invites a closer look at communities whose stories stretch far beyond recorded history. Proclaimed by the United Nations in 1994 and first observed in 1995, the day honours Indigenous Peoples worldwide. More than 476 million Indigenous people live across about 90 countries, sustaining thousands of cultures and many of the world's roughly 7,000 languages. In Canada, First Nations, Inuit and Métis peoples each have distinct histories, traditions and languages that continue to shape the country's identity.

copyright: Infinity Bridge in Stockton-on-Tees, England (© Bahadir Yeniceri/Shutterstock)
description: At first glance, it's just a bridge. Then the reflection changes everything. Infinity Bridge spans the River Tees in Stockton-on-Tees, England, where its two striking steel arches and their reflections create the shape of an infinity symbol, inspiring its name. Opened in 2009, the pedestrian and cycle bridge was designed by Expedition Engineering with architect Spence Associates as part of the regeneration of the town's riverside. Stretching about 240 metres, its tied-arch structure combines engineering efficiency with a distinctive appearance.

copyright: Lime Kiln Lighthouse on San Juan Island, Washington state, United States (© Edmund Lowe Photography/Shutterstock)
description: Ships, storms and changing technology have come and gone, but the light remains. On Washington's San Juan Island, Lime Kiln Lighthouse has overlooked Haro Strait since 1919. Perched on a rocky bluff, its white flash continues to guide vessels through a major inland marine waterway in the Pacific Northwest. The lighthouse stands within Lime Kiln Point State Park, which is recognised as one of the world's best places to watch wild orcas from shore, with whales sometimes passing remarkably close to the coast.

copyright: Edmonton at night, Alberta (© Tetyana Babiy/iStock/Getty Images)
description: The best seats don't have seat numbers. They start with a blanket spread out on the hill and someone nearby trying to guess the first song of the evening while sharing snacks. Sound familiar? It must be Folk Fest. From today until 9 August, Gallagher Park once again becomes a gathering place for Edmonton music lovers. What keeps people coming back year after year? It's rarely just one artist. Across the festival's stages, musicians perform solo sets, then join others for workshop sessions that create one-off collaborations.

copyright: Decorated gate of the Royal Palace of Fez, Morocco (© cgst26/Shutterstock)
description: In Fez, Morocco, the Royal Palace—known as Dar al-Makhzen—has stood as a seat of power since the 13th century, when Morocco's rulers established a fortified royal city around it. Behind its high walls lie gardens, courtyards, mosques and royal residences spread across a vast complex still used by the king today, making it both historic and fully active.
